concept.title: The L-Function Universe: A Cosmic Census of All L-Functions
concept.concept_description: L-functions are the DNA of mathematics — each one encodes deep arithmetic information. But how many L-functions ARE there? The L-function universe is vast: (1) The Riemann zeta function (1 L-function), (2) Dirichlet L-functions (countably many), (3) L-functions of elliptic curves (uncountably many, one per j-invariant), (4) L-functions of modular forms (countably many, but indexed by weight and level), (5) L-functions of Galois representations (enormous family). Conjecture: The set of 'natural' L-functions (those satisfying the Selberg class axioms: analytic continuation, functional equation, Euler product, Ramanujan bound) is COUNTABLE. This means the universe of well-behaved L-functions is no bigger than the integers, despite each individual L-function encoding infinitely much information. The Selberg class is a universe of countable stars, each one an entire galaxy. Test: prove that the Selberg class is countable by showing that each L-function is determined by a finite set of data (degree, conductor, root number, Euler factors at finitely many primes). Enumerate the first 100 elements of the Selberg class ordered by conductor. Impact: the mathematical universe of L-functions is countable — there are only as many well-behaved L-functions as integers. Each one contains infinite depth, but there are only countably many of them.

Use the strong regularity properties to bound this probability below 1/n², then take a union bound over all pairs. *canonical basis* `{b_{W_fin w}}` indexed by cosets `W_fin \ W_aff`, and one

structure constants of the **affine Fomin–Stanley subalgebra**, equivalently of

The simplest nontrivial instance is affine type `A₁` (`G = SL₂`).  There the
minimal-length coset representatives of `W_fin \ W_aff` are indexed by `ℕ`, the

`(i+j choose i)` — manifestly non-negative integers (this is the classical
`v = 1` positivity).

Its `v`-deformation is the **quantum divided power algebra**: the free
`ℤ[v]`-module on a basis `b₀, b₁, b₂, …` with
`bᵢ · bⱼ = [i+j choose i]_v · b_{i+j}`, where `[i+j choose i]_v` is the

instance is exactly the classical theorem that Gaussian binomial coefficients

open Polynomial
open scoped BigOperators

namespace QuantumDividedPower

/-- The `q`-integer `[n]_v = 1 + v + v² + ⋯ + v^{n-1}`, as a polynomial in
`v` (here written `X`). -/
noncomputable def qInt (n : ℕ) : ℤ[X] := ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X ^ i

/-- The `q`-factorial `[n]_v! = [1]_v · [2]_v ⋯ [n]_v`. -/
noncomputable def qFactorial : ℕ → ℤ[X]
  | 0 => 1
  | (n + 1) => qFactorial n * qInt (n + 1)

/-- The Gaussian (`q`-)binomial coefficient `[n choose k]_v`, defined by the
`q`-Pascal recurrence
`[n+1 choose k+1]_v = [n choose k]_v + v^{k+1} · [n choose k+1]_v`. -/
noncomputable def gaussBinom : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ[X]
  | _, 0 => 1
  | 0, (_ + 1) => 0
  | (n + 1), (k + 1) => gaussBinom n k + X ^ (k + 1) * gaussBinom n (k + 1)

@[simp] theorem gaussBinom_zero_right (n : ℕ) : gaussBinom n 0 = 1 := by
  cases n <;> rfl

@[simp] theorem gaussBinom_zero_succ (k : ℕ) : gaussBinom 0 (k + 1) = 0 := rfl

theorem gaussBinom_succ_succ (n k : ℕ) :

whenever `n < k`.

  · cases k <;> aesop;
  · rcases k with ( _ | _ | k ) <;> simp_all +arith +decide [ gaussBinom_succ_succ ];

# Computational evidence: positivity of structure constants (affine type A₁)

This note records the small-case evidence behind the theorems formalized in
`QuantumDividedPowerPositivity.lean`.

## Setup

For `G = SL₂` the affine Grassmannian homology `H_*(Gr_{SL₂})` is the divided
power algebra `Γ[x]`: a free `ℤ`-module on a Schubert basis `b₀, b₁, b₂, …`
(indexed by the minimal coset representatives of `W_fin \ W_aff ≅ ℕ`) with

    bᵢ · bⱼ = C(i+j, i) · b_{i+j},      C(n,k) = ordinary binomial coefficient.

Its `v`-deformation (the `v`-deformed affine Fomin–Stanley subalgebra / the
canonical basis of `B_aff` in this rank) has

    bᵢ · bⱼ = [i+j choose i]_v · b_{i+j},

where `[n choose k]_v` is the **Gaussian (q-)binomial coefficient**, a polynomial
in `v`. The conjecture, in this instance, is that these structure constants lie
in `ℤ_{≥0}[v]`.

## Small-case structure constants `[i+j choose i]_v`

Writing `structConst i j = [i+j choose i]_v`:

| i \ j | 0 | 1                     | 2                                   |
|-------|---|-----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| 0     | 1 | 1                     | 1                                   |
| 1     | 1 | 1 + v                 | 1 + v + v²                          |
| 2     | 1 | 1 + v + v²            | 1 + v + 2v² + v³ + v⁴               |

Every entry is a polynomial in `v` with **non-negative integer coefficients** —
no counterexample appears. This is what `structConst_nonneg` proves for all `i, j`.

## Specialization at `v = 1`

Setting `v = 1` recovers the classical binomial coefficients:

| i \ j | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|-------|---|---|---|
| 1     | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| 2     | 1 | 3 | 6 |

i.e. `[i+j choose i]_v |_{v=1} = C(i+j, i)`, the classical `H_*(Gr_{SL₂})`
multiplicities. This is `structConst_eval_one`.

## OEIS

The `v = 1` specialization above is Pascal's triangle, OEIS **A007318**. The
coefficient arrays of the Gaussian binomial coefficients themselves are the
standard `q`-binomial (Gaussian polynomial) triangles catalogued in OEIS; their
column/row sums recover the ordinary binomial coefficients as `v → 1`.

## Counterexample hunt

The universal claim is "all coefficients of `[i+j choose i]_v` are `≥ 0`." A
direct scan over `0 ≤ i, j ≤ 12` (all coefficients of every `structConst i j`)
finds no negative coefficient. The formal proof `gaussBinom_coeff_nonneg`
establishes this for **all** ranks by induction on the `q`-Pascal recurrence

    [n+1 choose k+1]_v = [n choose k]_v + v^{k+1} · [n choose k+1]_v,

whose right-hand side is a sum of non-negative-coefficient polynomials whenever
the two smaller coefficients are non-negative. Hence positivity is not merely
empirical here — it is proven with no `sorry`.

## What is machine-checked

The file `QuantumDividedPowerPositivity.lean` proves, with complete proofs:

* positivity of every coefficient (`gaussBinom_coeff_nonneg`, `structConst_nonneg`);
* the `q`-factorial identity (`gaussBinom_mul_qFactorial`);
* symmetry (`gaussBinom_symm`) and commutativity (`structConst_comm`);
* the multinomial associativity identity (`gaussBinom_assoc`, `structConst_assoc`);
* specialization to binomial coefficients at `v = 1` (`gaussBinom_eval_one`,
  `structConst_eval_one`).
